ch35.d.d: Distance $d$ between the centres of the two slits
ch35.d.lambda: Wavelength $\lambda$ of the incoming light, shown as its colour
ch35.d.D: Distance $D$ from the slits to the screen
ch35.d.yp: Screen point for the two paths; drag the white dot on the screen
ch35.goal.path: Brightness on the screen is set by the path difference $\Delta L$ of the waves from the two slits: whole wavelengths add, half wavelengths cancel
ch35.goal.spacing: Bright-fringe spacing $\Delta y \approx \lambda D/d$: proportional to the wavelength, inversely proportional to the slit separation
ch35.obs.build: Play: the plane wave reaches the slits, two circular waves spread and overlap, and the screen accumulates the time-averaged intensity until the fringes and the intensity graph appear
ch35.obs.marker: Drag the white dot on the screen: $\Delta L/\lambda$ = 0, 1, 2, … on bright fringes and 0.5, 1.5, … on dark fringes
ch35.obs.nodal: Gaps in the wavefronts (nodal lines): crest meets trough and the waves always cancel; they run from the slits to the dark fringes. Across a nodal line the wavefronts shift by half a wavelength
ch35.obs.lambda: Wavelength 400 → 700 nm: the fringes spread apart
ch35.obs.d: Slit separation 2 → 4 μm: the fringes move closer together
ch35.assume.model: 2D model: each slit is one Huygens point source (a very narrow slit), amplitude $\propto r^{-1/2}$, no reflection from the barrier. The diffraction envelope of slits with a width is in Ch 36 tab 1 (two slits)
ch35.assume.scale: Slit separation and screen distance are scaled down to μm to fit the stage. Real set-ups have $D \gg d$, where $\Delta y = \lambda D/d$ becomes exact. Here $\Delta y$ (mark and readout) is the exact first bright fringe, $\Delta L = \lambda$
ch35.assume.colour: Lines are wavefronts (crests); their strength is the amplitude relative to the brightest point at the same distance (left out near nodal lines). The intensity graph is relative to the central maximum
